dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation

evidence.note: Read every source file, located exec_one and identified which functions are stubbed vs buggy (exec_numeric, Call/CallIndirect unimplemented; validate_module a no-op stub; block/branch broken); built baseline to confirm what compiles.
Enumerated the 0xFD SIMD prefix sub-opcode numbering from the SIMD spec before implementing families — orientation to the binary encoding.
Probed exact spec-test cases with struct.unpack to disambiguate trunc-conversion bounds and round-half-to-even nearest semantics rather than guessing.
Repeatedly used wasm2wat (wabt) to inspect actual test binaries, confirming encoding, lane-order and type assumptions against generated output.
Sustained re-research when families (SIMD shifts, alignment, lane indices) behaved unexpectedly, pinning non-obvious semantics from spec/binaries.

Rewrote runtime.rs from scratch and modified spec.rs despite the frozen-contract instruction — orientation to the fixed public API was understood but imperfectly honored, keeping it short of a clean 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent exhibits all level-8 behaviors — an explicit map of what compiles, which MVP functions are stubbed/buggy, where value types/decoding/memory/execution are wired, and the 0xFD encoding — and pins non-obvious semantics (saturation, NaN/nearest, conversion bounds, lane order) from the spec. It also shows the level-10 hallmarks: sustained targeted re-research per family, probing specific spec-test cases, and confirming encoding against wabt output. It falls just short of 10 because its orientation to the frozen public contract was imperfect (rewrote runtime.rs and edited spec.rs), so I place it at 9.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones

evidence.note: After exploration, the agent formed a coarse plan (implement exec_numeric, Call/CallIndirect, fix blocks, add V128 + all SIMD) but explicitly decided to write 'everything as one massive file' — a two-phase MVP+SIMD idea with no per-family milestone ordering or done-checks.

The entire runtime — MVP execution plus all SIMD families — was authored in one monolithic push (runtime.rs written in sequential appends, exec_simd_op2/op3/op4). SIMD was grouped by shape (i8x16, i16x8, i32x4...) in the CODE, showing family awareness, but there was no 'implement one family, run its spec test, move on' loop.

Agent enumerated SIMD sub-opcode ranges by family (swizzle, splat, comparisons per shape). This is family-level structural awareness, but it fed a single big implementation rather than an ordered, checkpointed milestone plan.
First real verification was a broad 'run all tests' at 95.93%, not per-family checkpoints hit as each family was completed — verification came after the whole monolith, not milestone-by-milestone.

The back half was reactive triage: fix failures found in call_indirect, global, memory, simd_align, simd_lane, simd_load8_lane one file at a time. Each json acted as a rough per-file done-check, but this was failure-driven cleanup, not a pre-planned dependency-ordered family milestone hierarchy.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent held a genuine two-phase MVP-then-SIMD conception and organized SIMD by shape families in the code (above anchor 3's 'no sub-structure'), but it did NOT implement family-by-family with each family's spec test as a checkpoint — it wrote one monolithic runtime covering all families at once, then verified in aggregate and fixed failures reactively file-by-file. That falls short of anchor 5's 'implementing family by family with the matching spec test as a rough checkpoint,' with no dependency-aware ordered milestone plan or per-family pass targets set in advance. This lands between the vague-two-phase (3) and the family-by-family-checkpointed (5) anchors, at 4.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification

evidence.note: Built early, ran i32.json to establish a baseline, then looped over all family jsons reading FAIL lines to localize where failures concentrated (assert_invalid) rather than assuming correctness.

Drilled into individual failing assertions to diagnose semantic edge cases: f64 trunc bound at -2147483648.9, round-half-to-even for nearest (-0.5→-0), and 'undefined' vs 'uninitialized' element trap text — exactly the NaN/sign/boundary diagnosis the top anchor describes.

After adding the validator, spotted an MVP regression (pass rate crashed to 31%), investigated per-file, and confirmed i32 back to green while re-checking SIMD — guarding MVP against regression on integration.
Used per-family SIMD jsons (simd_bit_shift) to localize a mis-categorized shift opcode range, and distinguished a decoder encoding bug (mutability byte) from validator type-checks.

Iterated per-family (simd_align, simd_lane, simd_load8_lane) fixing alignment and lane-index validation, treating the aggregate 99.8x% as a monitored signal and driving to an exact 1.0 before submitting.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran a disciplined implement→run family json→read specific FAIL@line→fix→re-run loop, periodically running aggregate loops over all files to catch regressions (matching the level-8 anchor), and went further: it drilled into individual assertions to diagnose NaN/rounding, saturation/trunc boundaries, sign, and lane-order edge cases, distinguished genuine bugs from encoding mismatches, guarded MVP against validator regressions, and treated the aggregate score as a continuously monitored signal it pushed to an exact 1.0. This is the full engineered-verification behavior described by the level-10 anchor.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface

evidence.note: Ran full/per-file suites, tracked 95.93% pass rate, and explicitly counted failure types (assert_invalid=1375, trap=10, return=5, malformed=4), identifying the validator as the highest-remaining bucket and reallocating effort there.
Detected a regression: after adding the validator, pass rate collapsed to 31% and SIMD modules stopped loading — noticed a fix in one family breaking others and traced it to missing SIMD validation.
Continuously reconciled aggregate score (96.5% -> 99.8% -> 99.83%), quantified remaining gap ('70 failures left'), and drove toward 1.0.
Methodically enumerated each remaining failing file (call_indirect, global, simd_align, simd_lane, simd_load8_lane), knowing precisely what remained per family until reaching 100%.
Spent ~12 steps circling on the call_indirect panic, re-running the same case repeatedly before diagnosing — mild loss of momentum on a single blocked case rather than a maintained blocked-ledger.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent continuously reconciled the aggregate score against categorized per-family failure counts, quantified the concrete gap to 1.0, reallocated effort toward the highest-remaining family (validator/assert_invalid), and detected when a fix in one area (the validator) regressed another (SIMD) — all hallmarks of the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because it kept no explicit maintained done/remaining/blocked ledger and briefly circled on the call_indirect panic rather than catching that stall immediately.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Recognized the lane-immediate-packed-in-MemArg.offset representation was 'hacky' and considered a cleaner dedicated Instr variant, but chose to barrel ahead with the messy hack rather than rework the foundation — the anti-pattern for this dimension (later forced special-case lane validation on top of it).

After noticing assert_invalid failures dominate (1375 of them) and that per-test patching couldn't reach 1.0, stepped back and added an entirely new validate.rs type-checker — a structural response to the root generator of failures, flipping many downstream assertions.

When the new validator regressed SIMD tests (dropped to 31%, rejecting valid modules), correctly diagnosed that the validator skipped SIMD ops and added SIMD validation rather than reverting or patching individual tests.

When SIMD shift families stubbornly failed, traced root cause to a miscategorized opcode range (107-109 wrongly in the binary v128,v128 list) in the shared validate_simd_other helper and chose to completely rewrite the categorization function once, rather than patch each family — fixing the generator of failures.
Recognized the trunc bounds were semantically wrong (rejecting valid -2147483648.9) and corrected the underlying bound formula rather than special-casing the failing test.
Mostly local safety patches for panics (bounds-checked indexing, memory limit checks, trap-message tweaks) — legitimate but surface-level fixes rather than structural rethinks.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly hit the 8-anchor behavior: it recognized when a failure signaled a structural problem — adding a whole validator module when assert_invalid dominated, and rewriting the miscategorized shared validate_simd_other helper once so many families flipped together — rather than piling per-instance patches. However, it is pulled below a clean 8 by a notable counterexample: it consciously identified the lane-in-offset value representation as messy yet chose to barrel ahead rather than rework it, and much of the mid-game was surface patching. The reactive (not proactive) nature and the un-reworked hacky representation keep it short of 8-10, so a 7 best captures the interpolation between 'reconsiders when a family fails' and 'refactors the shared cause once.'

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon systems task: understand an existing partial Rust WASM interpreter, fix its bugs/unimplemented MVP functions, then add the entire 128-bit SIMD proposal — hundreds of opcodes across ~15 semantic families (memory, splat, lane, bitwise, int/float arith, saturating, widen/narrow, conversions, dot, q15). Difficulty comes from breadth (must not lose track), subtle exact semantics (saturation, NaN, rounding, lane order), a hard fixed-interface constraint, and an all-or-nothing 1.0 target measured by a provided per-assertion spec-test harness. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, family-level decomposition, and tight incremental verification.

dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the provided skeleton (Value model, decode/runtime/types, which functions are stubbed or buggy, the fixed public contract) and the SIMD binary encoding + lane semantics before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task forbids rewriting and forbids touching spec.rs/main.rs or renaming public items; wrong assumptions about the existing Value representation or the 0xFD encoding propagate into every one of hundreds of opcodes. Getting exact per-family semantics (lane order, sat, NaN) is a research act, not guesswork.

anchors.0: Starts editing/adding opcodes without reading the existing sources or the spec-test format; invents an interface.
anchors.3: Skims one or two files; knows it's a WASM interpreter but not which functions are stubbed vs buggy, nor how v128 must slot into the existing Value type.
anchors.5: Reads decode.rs/runtime.rs/types.rs and identifies the public items that must not change, the existing value/stack model, and roughly how the 0xFD prefix + LEB sub-opcode is decoded; consults spec semantics for the common families.
anchors.8: Builds an explicit map of the codebase: what compiles, which MVP functions are unimplemented/buggy, exactly where value types, decoding, memory, and execution are wired, and how v128 must integrate without breaking the frozen interface. Pins down non-obvious semantics (saturation, NaN propagation, signed/unsigned lanes, extend low/high ordering) from the spec rather than guessing.
anchors.10: All of the above plus sustained, targeted re-research when a family behaves unexpectedly: probes specific spec-test cases to disambiguate encoding/rounding/lane-order questions, verifies the fixed public API surface concretely, and confirms encoding assumptions against wabt-generated output — orientation continually deepens as unfamiliar families are reached.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — first MVP correctness, then SIMD by instruction family — each milestone tied to a concrete spec-test json as its done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are hundreds of opcodes but a clean natural structure (MVP first; then per-family, each with its own spec_json file). Treating it as one undifferentiated push guarantees losing the plot and thrashing across unrelated failures.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random opcodes with no ordering or notion of completion.
anchors.3: Vague two-phase idea ('do MVP then SIMD') with no sub-structure and no per-family done criteria.
anchors.5: Sequences MVP before SIMD and groups SIMD into a handful of families, implementing family by family with the matching spec test as a rough checkpoint.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ordered plan over the ~15 families with sensible dependency ordering (e.g. v128 value type + const/load/store and lane infra before arithmetic that depends on them), each milestone bound to a specific spec_json and a pass target, adjusted as families reveal shared infrastructure.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone hierarchy: shared primitives (lane read/write, splat, per-shape iteration helpers) are sequenced first to avoid rework, families ordered by leverage, each with an explicit exit check, and the structure is revised as reality shifts scope — never a flat undifferentiated list, never redundant re-implementation across families.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided spec-test harness at fine granularity — per-family json files and the aggregate runner — to localize failures and confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 1.0 (all-assertions) target is unforgiving; the harness reports per-assertion pass/fail per file, so a strategy of running individual family jsons and reading FAIL lines is the difference between fast localization and blind flailing across a giant surface.

anchors.0: Never builds/runs the tests, or only at the very end; declares done without evidence.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads only the final pass rate, without isolating which assertions fail or why.
anchors.5: Builds and runs the relevant per-family spec-test json after implementing each family, and uses FAIL lines to fix that family before moving on.
anchors.8: Systematic loop: implement family → run its json → read specific FAIL @ line reasons → fix → re-run to green, and periodically runs the full runner to confirm no regressions, keeping MVP files passing while adding SIMD.
anchors.10: Verification is engineered: drills into individual failing assertions to diagnose semantic edge cases (NaN, saturation boundaries, sign, lane order), distinguishes genuine bugs from encoding mismatches, guards against MVP regressions on every integration, and treats the aggregate score as a monitored signal rather than a one-shot final check — pursuing the exact 1.0 rather than 'mostly passing'.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which families/opcodes are done, which remain, and which are stuck, across a very long implementation horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of opcodes and a strict 1.0 bar, an agent that loses track will either declare victory with families unimplemented or re-debug the same failing case in circles.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done vs remaining; forgets whole families or repeats work.
anchors.3: Rough mental sense of progress; frequently surprised by unimplemented opcodes or unnoticed regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of families and current pass counts, updating it as families complete, and generally knows what remains.
anchors.8: Continuously reconciles per-family pass counts and the aggregate score against the full opcode list, notices when a fix in one family breaks another, and detects when it is stuck on a single assertion rather than making progress.
anchors.10: Maintains a precise done/remaining/blocked ledger over the whole surface, catches thrashing early (same FAIL recurring), quantifies the remaining gap to 1.0 concretely, and reallocates effort toward the highest-remaining-assertion families instead of polishing already-green ones — the plot is never lost across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality diverges — e.g. a Value-type representation, decoding assumption, or semantic reading turns out wrong — rather than barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (how v128 is stored, how lanes are read, how memory ops share code) and semantic guesses (sat/NaN/lane order) are easy to get subtly wrong; the fixed-interface constraint can also force a rethink. Detecting and reworking these beats piling fixes on a broken foundation.

anchors.0: Keeps applying local patches to a broken assumption; never revisits the root cause even as failures persist.
anchors.3: Occasionally tweaks approach under pressure but mostly forces the original plan regardless of evidence.
anchors.5: When a family stubbornly fails, steps back and reconsiders the relevant assumption (encoding, representation, or semantics) and adjusts.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a structural problem (e.g. shared lane/decoding helper is wrong, or a value-representation choice can't satisfy the frozen interface) and refactors the shared cause once, so many downstream assertions flip together.
anchors.10: Proactively distinguishes root-cause divergence from surface bugs, reworks the foundation decisively and cleanly without breaking green families, and updates its plan/milestones to reflect the new understanding — demonstrably avoiding circular re-debugging by fixing the generator of failures rather than each instance.
